subject: VPC / On‑prem: burst engineering handoff & scaling play
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Sarah Kim <sarah@northstar.io>, BrightLane Ops <ops@brightlane.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: VPC / On‑prem: burst engineering handoff & scaling play

Team,

Following the BrightLane kickoff yesterday I pulled together a short play to hand off to infra + networking for the private GPU pool: our ask is to support a 3x short‑burst (90s median) above baseline sustained QPS for the first 48 hours of launch, with a fallback to a smaller quantized model in a different rack if we hit sustained queueing. Key specifics below — please treat as an engineering handoff (we need concrete runbook items, ownership, and a brief risk list):

Targets/assumptions:
- Baseline sustained qps per tenant: 120 qps at p95 latency 220ms (model: xform-11b-fp16).
- Burst target: absorb an additional 360 qps (3x) for 60–120s windows, 95th percentile of bursts expected in first 48h.
- Warm pools: aim to keep 20% of GPU slots warm for instant admission; warmup time (cold->ready) ~45s.

Networking constraints we think matter:
- Egress headroom: estimate 1.1Gbps per GPU during peak KV exchange; plan for NIC oversubscription <= 1.5x per top-of-rack to avoid packet drops.
- Peering: BGP convergence target <5s for route failover between racks.
- Congestion policy: apply token bucket policing at top-of-rack to prioritize KV/cache/backplane traffic for inference RPCs.

Operational mechanics we need from infra/networking:
1) Admission control policy that: rejects low-value large-batch requests during bursts, promotes latency SLOs.
2) Fast fallback chain: detect queuing > 500ms median per-request for 15s -> route to quantized variant (xform-11b-q4) or hosted fallback.
3) A warm-pool orchestration trigger (API + metric hook) we can call from rollout to pre-warm specified GPUs ahead of burst windows.
4) Observable signals in Console: per-GPU link utilization, queue depth distribution, grpc/rtx error rates, and per-tenant tokenized cost deltas.

Attachments: I dropped a short model of the burst profile (vpc-burst-model-params.xlsx) and a simplified topology png we used in the meeting.

Actions requested by EOD:
- Karthik: provide a short list of admission control knobs you prefer (timeouts, max-batches per-slot, per-tenant watermark) and a rough implementation ETA.
- Grace: confirm network egress allocation plan and NIC oversubscription limit you're comfortable shipping for the pilot.
- Laura: ops checklist for canary/cutover steps + quick rollback criteria.

I'll follow up with the BrightLane SREs if there are network-level asks that require their approval.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Product Manager, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, BrightLane Ops <ops@brightlane.ai>
Cc: Sarah Kim <sarah@northstar.io>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC / On‑prem: burst engineering handoff & scaling play

Marcus — quick response with the admission knobs I think are smallest lift:
- Max inflight per-GPU: token bucket that limits to N concurrent infer calls (we typically set N=12 for 80ms median tokens but will tune).
- Max batch size per-slot: hard cap at 8 for latency sensitive routes; allow larger on non‑latency routes.
- Backpressure signal: reject with explicit 429 + Retry-After when queue depth > 75% of slot capacity.

Implementation ETA: we can have a prototype in the staging cluster in 4 working days (ETA: Tue 20 Apr) if we scope to the grpc proxy/allocator layer only. Full rollout (with metric-driven auto-shed) will take ~3 weeks including safety tests.

Notes on fallback: prefer routing to quantized variant over hosted fallback for privacy guarantees; we should reserve a small set of racks with q4 models and pre-warm them via an orchestration hook.

I'll attach a short design sketch later today.

—Karthik
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, BrightLane Ops <ops@brightlane.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC / On‑prem: burst engineering handoff & scaling play

Thanks — reviewed the numbers. A few practical constraints from networking:
1) We can guarantee per-rack NIC oversubscription up to 1.4x by reserving VXLAN lanes and reducing other tenant best‑effort flows. 1.5x is risky given current backplane load.
2) BGP convergence: hardware supports <3s if we adjust keepalive timers, but that increases control-plane churn — happy to run a short test on staging.
3) Token bucket policing: we should prioritize UDP/GRPC ports tied to inference (50051/50052) and mark packets for QoS. We'll need a short ACL change from BrightLane (ops@brightlane.ai) — ops, can you confirm change window?

I also sketched a micro‑runbook for warm pools: warm-on-demand via an L2 API that accepts a list of tenantIDs + desired slot count; it returns a handle which will be useful for the rollout. I attached the topology + the checklist (network-topology-handoff.png and mh-tos-comm-checklist.pdf).

Grace
Head of Network Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightLane Ops <ops@brightlane.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC / On‑prem: burst engineering handoff & scaling play

Marking up the canary + rollback checklist now — high level:
- Canary window: 30 minutes with a gradually increasing traffic ramp (0 -> 50% -> 100% of planned baseline).
- Acceptance: p95 latency must not exceed baseline + 40% and error rate < 0.5% over the window.
- Rollback triggers: sustained queueing > 3x baseline for 2 consecutive minutes OR BGP neighbor flap > 3 within 10 minutes.
- Post-mortem triggers: any outage or SLA miss -> 1 business day turnaround for root cause and remediation plan.

I'll drop the checklist PDF to the Drive link. Ops — please confirm an outage window the BrightLane team can accept for the ACL change Grace mentioned.

—Laura (Ops)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Sarah Kim <sarah@northstar.io>, BrightLane Ops <ops@brightlane.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC / On‑prem: burst engineering handoff & scaling play

Great — appreciate the quick turn. Summarizing next steps and owners (please reply if anything missing):
- Karthik: prototype admission-control in staging by 2027-04-20 (deliverable: design sketch + staging runbook).
- Grace: confirm NIC oversubscription policy (target 1.4x) and get ACL change window from BrightLane ops (by EOD Thu 2027-04-15).
- Laura: post the canary checklist to Drive and confirm rollback play specifics (by Fri 2027-04-16).
- Marcus: I'll coordinate with BrightLane SRE for the ACL window and share the Drive link and HS record (HS-12345).

Risk callouts to keep in mind:
- If warm pool priming takes longer than estimated, we will see increased tail latency for the first burst — ensure orchestration hook has observable completion.
- If per‑rack oversubscription is higher than 1.4x we risk packet drops that will surface as grpc timeouts and queueing; fallback to quantized models should be tested end-to-end.

I'll close the loop when BrightLane confirms the ACL window.

Marcus
